newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Punishment sought for Venezuela jail fire culprits.
newsitem.headline: Punishment sought for Venezuela jail fire culprits.

text.p: Three National Guardsmen who seem to have deliberately started a fire that killed 25 inmates in a crowded Venezuelan jail cell must be brought to justice, officials and human rights groups said on Thursday.

"There's proof that these three guards locked the door, lobbed in tear gas canisters and that these set fire to the mattresses," Justice Minister Henrique Meier told Reuters in a brief telephone interview.
Meier said police tests had shown that the tear gas canisters had created the sparks that started Tuesday's fire at La Planta jail in southwestern Caracas.
"There is sufficient proof and the guilty must be punished," Meier said.

Prisoners have said the fire began after an argument broke out between inmates and guards during an early morning roll call. About 40 inmates were trapped inside the small cell. Some prisoners managed to crawl to safety through a small hole in the roof. The rest died engulfed in flames.
"It was a totally arbitrary, inhumane and unforgivable act," Meier said.

The mother of one victim said guards had told inmates last week they would carry out a massacre. "He told us that they were afraid because a guard told them he was going to burn them alive," Carmen Sanchez told Union Radio.

But rights activists said that even overwhelming evidence may not be enough to bring those responsible to justice. "Our fear is that after one to two years they will be free," Raul Cubas, general coordinator of local rights group Provea, told Reuters.
"As normally the justice here doesn't punish officials who violate human rights they don't fear the consequences of their actions," Cubas said.
Apart from the military trial, two civil courts have opened investigations into the tragedy, creating confusion and a conflict of interests, activists said.
The guards on duty at the time of the incident were arrested on Wednesday and placed at the disposition of a military judge.

Morgue officials said they had identified 19 of the 25 charred and twisted bodies recovered from the cell. "The causes of death were burns and suffocation although we still cannot say which came first," a morgue official told Reuters.

Criminal experts blamed the tragedy on critical overcrowding at the jail. Converted from an army barracks over 30 years ago to house 550 inmates, La Planta currently holds 1,700. About 70 percent of inmates have not been sentenced, officials said.

The presence of National Guardsmen within such an environment creates an explosive cocktail, Gomez added. The National Guard has provided additional security at Venezuela's violence-prone prisons for several years.
Venezuela's overcrowded and decaying prisons, considered to be among the most dangerous in Latin America, are frequent scenes of violence between inmates and clashes with guards.

The tragedy at La Planta was the worst in Venezuela's .tjails since about 120 prisoners were burned or hacked to death with machetes during a gang fight at the Sabaneta jail in the western city of Maracaibo in January 1994.
